decisions.choice: the ark of Yahweh: the chest that stood for Yahweh's presence, captured by the Philistines
decisions.reason: The Philistines had taken the ark in battle (4:11) and moved it from Ashdod to Gath to Ekron, and each city was struck with a plague (5:1-12). This chapter tells how they sent it back.

decisions.choice: territory of the Philistines: the whole Philistine country, not only open fields
decisions.reason: The word usually means "field", but it can name the open country or region belonging to a people (Genesis 32:4; Ruth 1:1). The ark had been in several Philistine cities, so the region as a whole is meant.

decisions.choice: the land of the Philistines (Balanced); Philistine territory (Readable)
decisions.reason: Both say plainly that the region is meant, not farmland.

source.text: וַיִּקְרְא֣וּ פְלִשְׁתִּ֗ים לַכֹּהֲנִ֤ים וְלַקֹּֽסְמִים֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר מַֽה־נַּעֲשֶׂ֖ה לַאֲר֣וֹן יְהוָ֑ה הוֹדִעֻ֕נוּ בַּמֶּ֖ה נְשַׁלְּחֶ֥נּוּ לִמְקוֹמֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And called [the] Philistines for the priests and for the diviners, saying, What shall we do with [the] ark of Yahweh? Make known to us with what we shall send it to its place.

en.L: And [the] Philistines called for the priests and for the diviners, saying, "What shall we do with the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}? Make known to us with what we shall send it to its place."
en.B: Then the Philistines summoned the priests and the diviners and said, "What should we do with the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}? Tell us what we should send with it when we send it back to its place."
en.R: Then the Philistines called for their priests and for the men who claimed to learn hidden things from signs. They asked, "What should we do with the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}? Tell us what we should send along with it when we send it back to where it belongs."

es.L: Y [los] filisteos llamaron a los sacerdotes y a los adivinos, diciendo: «¿Qué haremos con el arca {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}? {{plural_you:Hágannos|Hacednos}} saber con qué la enviaremos a su lugar».
es.B: Entonces los filisteos convocaron a los sacerdotes y a los adivinos y les dijeron: «¿Qué debemos hacer con el arca {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}? {{plural_you:Dígannos|Decidnos}} qué debemos enviar con ella cuando la devolvamos a su lugar».
es.R: Entonces los filisteos llamaron a sus sacerdotes y a los hombres que decían descubrir cosas ocultas por medio de señales. Les preguntaron: «¿Qué hacemos con el arca {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}? {{plural_you:Dígannos|Decidnos}} qué debemos mandar junto con ella cuando la devolvamos a su lugar».

fr.L: Et les Philistins appelèrent les prêtres et les devins, en disant : « Que ferons-nous de l’arche {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} ? Faites-nous savoir avec quoi nous la renverrons à sa place. »
fr.B: Les Philistins convoquèrent alors les prêtres et les devins et leur dirent : « Que devons-nous faire de l’arche {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} ? Dites-nous ce que nous devons envoyer avec elle quand nous la renverrons chez elle. »
fr.R: Alors les Philistins ont appelé leurs prêtres et les hommes qui prétendaient découvrir les choses cachées grâce à des signes. Ils leur ont demandé : « Que devons-nous faire de l’arche {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} ? Dites-nous ce que nous devons envoyer avec elle quand nous la renverrons là où elle doit être. »

vi.L: Người Phi-li-tin gọi các thầy tế lễ và các thầy bói mà nói: "Chúng ta phải làm gì với hòm của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}? Hãy cho chúng ta biết phải gửi hòm về chỗ của nó với vật gì."
vi.B: Người Phi-li-tin cho mời các thầy tế lễ và các thầy bói đến và hỏi: "Chúng ta phải làm gì với hòm của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}? Hãy cho chúng ta biết phải gửi gì theo khi đưa hòm về chỗ của nó."
vi.R: Người Phi-li-tin cho gọi các thầy tế lễ của họ và những người tự cho là đọc được điều bí ẩn qua các điềm lạ. Họ hỏi: "Chúng ta phải làm gì với hòm của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}? Hãy cho chúng ta biết phải gửi gì theo khi đưa hòm về nơi của nó."

decisions.choice: diviners: people who claimed to learn hidden things or the future from signs and omens
decisions.reason: Divination was common among Israel's neighbors and forbidden in Israel (Deuteronomy 18:10, 14). The Philistines call on their own religious experts to explain what has happened and what to do.

decisions.choice: with what: with what gift the ark should go back
alternatives: how shall we send it to its place?
decisions.reason: The question can mean "how" or "with what". The answer in verses 3-5, a guilt offering of gold sent along with the ark, shows that they are asking what should go with it.

decisions.choice: its place: the ark's own home among the Israelites
decisions.reason: The ark belonged with the people of the God of Israel, not in a Philistine temple (5:2-4, 11).

decisions.choice: the men who claimed to learn hidden things from signs
decisions.reason: Readable explains "diviners", a word many readers do not know, and says "their priests" because these are the Philistines' own priests.

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:Hágannos|Hacednos}}, {{plural_you:Dígannos|Decidnos}}
decisions.reason: The Philistines speak to the priests and diviners as a group, so the command takes the plural-you setting, as everywhere a group is addressed.

decisions.choice: "các thầy bói" (L, B) for the diviners; Readable explains, as the English does
decisions.reason: People who claimed to read hidden things from signs (meaning decision); "thầy bói" is the everyday Vietnamese word for such a person.

source.text: וַיֹּאמְר֗וּ אִֽם־מְשַׁלְּחִ֞ים אֶת־אֲר֨וֹן אֱלֹהֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אַל־תְּשַׁלְּח֤וּ אֹתוֹ֙ רֵיקָ֔ם כִּֽי־הָשֵׁ֥ב תָּשִׁ֛יבוּ ל֖וֹ אָשָׁ֑ם אָ֤ז תֵּרָֽפְאוּ֙ וְנוֹדַ֣ע לָכֶ֔ם לָ֛מָּה לֹא־תָס֥וּר יָד֖וֹ מִכֶּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And they said, If [you are] sending [the] ark of [the] God of Israel, do not send it empty, but surely return to him a guilt offering; then you will be healed, and it will be known to you why not turns aside his hand from you.

en.L: And they said, "If you [are] sending away the ark of the God of Israel, do not send it away empty, but you must surely return to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} a guilt offering. Then you will be healed, and it will be known to you why {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand does not turn aside from you."
en.B: They answered, "If you are sending the ark of the God of Israel away, you must not send it empty. Be sure to return a guilt offering to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Then you will be healed, and you will know why {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand has not been taken away from you."
en.R: They answered, "If you send away the ark of the God of Israel, do not send it back with nothing. You must send {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} a guilt offering to make up for the wrong you have done. Then you will be healed, and you will know why {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has kept on punishing you."

es.L: Y ellos dijeron: «Si {{plural_you:envían|enviáis}} el arca del Dios de Israel, no la {{plural_you:envíen|enviéis}} vacía, sino que sin falta {{plural_you:le devolverán|le devolveréis}} una ofrenda por la culpa. Entonces {{plural_you:serán sanados|seréis sanados}}, y {{plural_you:sabrán|sabréis}} por qué no se aparta de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} mano».
es.B: Ellos respondieron: «Si {{plural_you:van|vais}} a devolver el arca del Dios de Israel, no la {{plural_you:devuelvan|devolváis}} con las manos vacías. {{plural_you:Asegúrense|Aseguraos}} de devolverle una ofrenda por la culpa. Entonces {{plural_you:sanarán|sanaréis}}, y {{plural_you:sabrán|sabréis}} por qué {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} mano no se ha apartado de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}».
es.R: Ellos respondieron: «Si {{plural_you:devuelven|devolvéis}} el arca del Dios de Israel, no la {{plural_you:manden|mandéis}} sin nada. {{plural_you:Tienen|Tenéis}} que enviarle una ofrenda por la culpa para reparar el mal que {{plural_you:han hecho|habéis hecho}}. Entonces {{plural_you:sanarán|sanaréis}}, y {{plural_you:sabrán|sabréis}} por qué {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} {{plural_you:los|os}} ha seguido castigando».

fr.L: Et ils dirent : « Si vous renvoyez l’arche du Dieu d’Israël, ne la renvoyez pas à vide, mais ne manquez pas de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} rendre un sacrifice de réparation. Alors vous serez guéris, et vous saurez pourquoi {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} main ne se détourne pas de vous. »
fr.B: Ils répondirent : « Si vous renvoyez l’arche du Dieu d’Israël, ne la renvoyez pas les mains vides. Ne manquez pas de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} offrir un sacrifice de réparation. Alors vous serez guéris, et vous saurez pourquoi {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} main ne s’est pas retirée de vous. »
fr.R: Ils ont répondu : « Si vous renvoyez l’arche du Dieu d’Israël, ne la renvoyez pas sans rien. Vous devez {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} envoyer une offrande de réparation pour réparer le mal que vous avez fait. Alors vous serez guéris, et vous saurez pourquoi {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a continué à vous punir. »

vi.L: Họ nói: "Nếu các ông gửi hòm của Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên đi, đừng gửi đi tay không, nhưng phải trả lại cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} một lễ vật chuộc lỗi. Bấy giờ các ông sẽ được chữa lành, và các ông sẽ biết vì sao tay {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} không rời khỏi các ông."
vi.B: Họ đáp: "Nếu các ông gửi hòm của Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên đi, thì không được gửi đi tay không. Phải trả lại cho vị thần ấy một lễ vật chuộc lỗi. Bấy giờ các ông sẽ được chữa lành, và sẽ biết vì sao tay vị thần ấy không rời khỏi các ông."
vi.R: Họ đáp: "Nếu các ông gửi hòm của Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên đi, thì đừng gửi đi mà không có gì. Các ông phải gửi cho vị thần ấy một lễ vật chuộc lỗi để đền bù điều sai trái các ông đã làm. Bấy giờ các ông sẽ được chữa lành, và các ông sẽ biết vì sao thần ấy cứ trừng phạt các ông mãi."

decisions.choice: guilt offering: a payment that makes up for a wrong done
decisions.reason: The word is the name of the guilt offering in Leviticus 5:14-26, where someone who has wronged what is holy pays it back and adds more. The Philistines had taken what belonged to Israel's God, so they return the ark with a payment of gold (verses 4-5, 8).

decisions.choice: his hand does not turn aside: he keeps on striking you
decisions.reason: "Hand" stands for God's power in action. In chapter 5 his hand was heavy on each city that held the ark (5:6, 7, 9, 11).

decisions.choice: you will know why his hand has not left you: once you are healed, it will be clear that his hand was the cause
alternatives: then you will be healed, and it will become known to you why his hand did not turn from you
and atonement will be made for you; will his hand not then turn from you?
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is short and can be read in more than one way. Read as it stands, healing after the offering will show that it was the God of Israel who had been striking them. The ancient Greek translation has "and atonement will be made for you; should not his hand then leave you?", which may reflect a different Hebrew text. The test in verse 9 takes up the same question of whether his hand was really the cause.

decisions.choice: a guilt offering to make up for the wrong you have done; he has kept on punishing you
decisions.reason: Readable explains what a guilt offering is for and says plainly what "his hand has not turned aside" means.

decisions.choice: "un sacrifice de réparation" (Literal, Balanced); "une offrande de réparation" (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Pentateuch note's term for the guilt offering, which says what it is for, making up for a wrong (m1). Here it is gold objects, not an animal, so Readable says "offrande".

decisions.choice: "una ofrenda por la culpa"
decisions.reason: The Pentateuch's term is "el sacrificio por la culpa"; here the Philistines' gift is gold objects, not an animal (m1), so the Spanish keeps the term's "por la culpa" with "ofrenda", the wider word.

decisions.choice: "lễ vật chuộc lỗi" for the guilt offering
decisions.reason: A payment that makes up for a wrong (meaning decision); "chuộc lỗi" keeps it apart from the sin offering. The Philistine priests call the Philistines "các ông" and speak of Israel's God as "vị thần ấy" at Balanced and Readable, as in 5:7.
