Le même fléau a frappé tout votre peuple et vos princes.

vi.L: Họ hỏi: "Lễ vật chuộc lỗi mà chúng tôi phải trả lại cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} [là] gì?" Họ đáp: "[Theo] số các lãnh chúa Phi-li-tin, năm cái bướu bằng vàng và năm con chuột bằng vàng, vì cùng một tai vạ [đã giáng] trên tất cả họ và trên các lãnh chúa của các ông.
vi.B: Họ hỏi: "Chúng tôi phải trả lại cho vị thần ấy lễ vật chuộc lỗi gì?" Các thầy đáp: "Năm cái bướu bằng vàng và năm con chuột bằng vàng, mỗi lãnh chúa Phi-li-tin một cái, vì cùng một tai vạ đã giáng trên cả dân lẫn các lãnh chúa của các ông.
vi.R: Người Phi-li-tin hỏi: "Chúng tôi phải gửi lễ vật chuộc lỗi gì cho vị thần ấy?" Các thầy tế lễ và thầy bói đáp: "Hãy gửi năm cái bướu bằng vàng và năm con chuột bằng vàng, mỗi lãnh chúa Phi-li-tin một cái. Cùng một tai vạ đã giáng trên toàn dân các ông và trên các lãnh chúa của các ông.

decisions.choice: rulers of the Philistines: the lords of the five Philistine cities
decisions.reason: This title is used only for the Philistine rulers. There were five of them, one each for Gaza, Ashdod, Ashkelon, Gath and Ekron (verse 17; Joshua 13:3; Judges 3:3).

decisions.choice: tumors: swellings on the body
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew text here, as in 5:6-12 and 6:5, has a word that means "mounds" or "swellings". The scribes' tradition for reading aloud replaces it with another word for tumors or swellings, perhaps a more polite one. Either way the plague caused painful swellings. What disease it was is not certain; some think of the swellings of bubonic plague, which rats spread, and the older word "emerods" (hemorrhoids) reflects another guess.

decisions.choice: rats: rodents that were ruining the land (verse 5)
decisions.reason: The word names a small rodent, a mouse or a rat; the language does not separate the two. Since these creatures were destroying the land (verse 5) and the plague brought swellings, a rat plague is likely, but the word itself does not settle which animal is meant.

decisions.choice: all of them and your rulers: the whole people and their rulers alike
decisions.reason: The speakers shift from "them" to "your". "All of them" is the Philistine people, and the same plague struck the rulers too, so each ruler sends an offering for his city.

decisions.choice: one for each of the rulers; all the people
decisions.reason: "The number of the rulers" means one gold image for each ruler, which Balanced and Readable say plainly. Both say "the people" for "all of them", and Readable names who is speaking in each half of the verse.

decisions.choice: "chuột" for the rodents
decisions.reason: The general Vietnamese word for rats and mice, as the meaning decision leaves the kind open.

source.text: וַעֲשִׂיתֶם֩ צַלְמֵ֨י טְחֹרֵיכֶ֜ם וְצַלְמֵ֣י עַכְבְּרֵיכֶ֗ם הַמַּשְׁחִיתִם֙ אֶת־הָאָ֔רֶץ וּנְתַתֶּ֛ם לֵאלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל כָּב֑וֹד אוּלַ֗י יָקֵ֤ל אֶת־יָדוֹ֙ מֵֽעֲלֵיכֶ֔ם וּמֵעַ֥ל אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֖ם וּמֵעַ֥ל אַרְצְכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will make images of your tumors and images of your mice that are ruining the land, and you will give to [the] God of Israel glory; perhaps he will lighten his hand from on you and from on your gods and from on your land.

en.L: And you will make images of your tumors and images of your rats that are ruining the land, and you will give glory to the God of Israel. Perhaps {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will lighten {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand from on you and from on your gods and from on your land.
en.B: So make images of your tumors and images of your rats that are destroying the land, and give glory to the God of Israel. Perhaps {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will lighten {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand on you, on your gods and on your land.
en.R: Make gold models of your tumors and of the rats that are ruining your land. In this way, give honor to the God of Israel. Then perhaps {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will stop punishing you and your gods and your land so heavily.

es.L: Y {{plural_you:harán|haréis}} imágenes de {{plural_you:sus tumores|vuestros tumores}} e imágenes de {{plural_you:sus ratas|vuestras ratas}} que destruyen la tierra, y {{plural_you:darán|daréis}} gloria al Dios de Israel. Quizá aligere {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} mano de sobre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, y de sobre {{plural_you:sus dioses|vuestros dioses}}, y de sobre {{plural_you:su tierra|vuestra tierra}}.
es.B: Así que {{plural_you:hagan|haced}} imágenes de {{plural_you:sus tumores|vuestros tumores}} y de las ratas que están destruyendo la tierra, y {{plural_you:den|dad}} gloria al Dios de Israel. Quizá aligere {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} mano sobre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, sobre {{plural_you:sus dioses|vuestros dioses}} y sobre {{plural_you:su tierra|vuestra tierra}}.
es.R: {{plural_you:Hagan|Haced}} figuras de oro de {{plural_you:sus tumores|vuestros tumores}} y de las ratas que están arruinando {{plural_you:su tierra|vuestra tierra}}. De ese modo {{plural_you:honren|honrad}} al Dios de Israel. Quizá así deje de {{plural_you:castigarlos|castigaros}} tan duramente a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, a {{plural_you:sus dioses|vuestros dioses}} y a {{plural_you:su tierra|vuestra tierra}}.

fr.L: Et vous ferez des images de vos tumeurs et des images de vos rats qui ravagent le pays, et vous donnerez gloire au Dieu d’Israël. Peut-être {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} allégera {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} main de dessus vous, et de dessus vos dieux, et de dessus votre pays.
fr.B: Faites donc des images de vos tumeurs et des images des rats qui dévastent le pays, et rendez gloire au Dieu d’Israël. Peut-être allégera-t-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} main qui pèse sur vous, sur vos dieux et sur votre pays.
fr.R: Faites des modèles en or de vos tumeurs et des rats qui ravagent votre pays. Ainsi, vous rendrez honneur au Dieu d’Israël. Alors peut-être qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} arrêtera de vous punir si durement, vous, vos dieux et votre pays.

vi.L: Các ông hãy làm hình các cái bướu của các ông và hình các con chuột đang phá hại xứ, và dâng vinh quang cho Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên. Biết đâu {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ làm nhẹ tay {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} trên các ông, trên các thần của các ông và trên xứ các ông.
vi.B: Vậy hãy làm hình các cái bướu và hình những con chuột đang phá hoại xứ sở các ông, và tôn vinh Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên. Biết đâu vị thần ấy sẽ nhẹ tay với các ông, với các thần của các ông và với xứ các ông.
vi.R: Hãy làm mô hình bằng vàng của các cái bướu và của những con chuột đang phá hại xứ các ông. Làm như vậy là tôn vinh Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên. Biết đâu vị thần ấy sẽ thôi trừng phạt nặng nề các ông, các thần của các ông và xứ các ông.

decisions.choice: the rats that are ruining the land: rodents swarming over Philistine country
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text of chapter 5 speaks only of tumors; the rats appear for the first time here, as if the reader already knows of them. The ancient Greek translation mentions mice spreading through the land already in 5:6 and 6:1.

decisions.choice: give glory to the God of Israel: openly admit his power and that he has been wronged
decisions.reason: To give glory to God can mean to confess the truth before him (Joshua 7:19). The gold images admit that the plague came from him. The word "glory" is related to "heavy": his hand was heavy on them (5:6, 11), and now they honor him so that he will make it light.

decisions.choice: lighten his hand: ease the punishment
decisions.reason: The picture of a heavy hand pressing down on someone (5:6, 11) is turned around: they hope he will lift its weight.

decisions.choice: your gods: the Philistine gods, Dagon among them
decisions.reason: Dagon's image had fallen and broken before the ark (5:2-5), so the speakers count their own gods among those struck.

decisions.choice: gold models; honor
decisions.reason: Readable says "models" for "images" and adds that they are gold, as verse 4 says. It uses "honor" for "glory", which here means showing respect.

source.text: וְלָ֤מָּה תְכַבְּדוּ֙ אֶת־לְבַבְכֶ֔ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֧ר כִּבְּד֛וּ מִצְרַ֥יִם וּפַרְעֹ֖ה אֶת־לִבָּ֑ם הֲלוֹא֙ כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר הִתְעַלֵּ֣ל בָּהֶ֔ם וַֽיְשַׁלְּח֖וּם וַיֵּלֵֽכוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And why will you make heavy your heart as made heavy Egypt and Pharaoh their heart? Was it not when he dealt harshly with them, and they sent them away, and they went?

en.L: And why will you make your heart heavy, just as Egypt and Pharaoh made their heart heavy? Was it not when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had dealt harshly with them that they sent them away, and they went?
en.B: Why harden your hearts the way the Egyptians and Pharaoh hardened theirs? Once {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had dealt harshly with them, did they not let the Israelites go, and they left?
en.R: Do not be stubborn the way the Egyptians and Pharaoh were. After God had punished them severely, they let the Israelites go, and the Israelites left Egypt.

es.L: ¿Y por qué {{plural_you:endurecerán|endureceréis}} {{plural_you:su corazón|vuestro corazón}}, como Egipto y el faraón endurecieron su corazón? ¿No fue cuando {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} los trató con dureza que los dejaron ir, y se fueron?
es.B: ¿Por qué {{plural_you:endurecer su corazón|endurecer vuestro corazón}} como lo endurecieron los egipcios y el faraón? Después de que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} los trató con dureza, ¿no dejaron ir a los israelitas, y estos se fueron?
es.R: No {{plural_you:sean|seáis}} tercos como lo fueron los egipcios y el faraón. Después de que Dios los castigó duramente, dejaron ir a los israelitas, y los israelitas salieron de Egipto.

fr.L: Et pourquoi endurciriez-vous votre cœur comme l’Égypte et Pharaon ont endurci leur cœur ? N’est-ce pas quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les eut maltraités qu’ils les laissèrent partir, et ils s’en allèrent ?
fr.B: Pourquoi endurcir votre cœur comme les Égyptiens et Pharaon ont endurci le leur ? Après qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les eut durement traités, n’ont-ils pas laissé partir les Israélites, qui s’en sont allés ?
fr.R: Ne soyez pas têtus comme les Égyptiens et Pharaon. Quand Dieu les a durement punis, ils ont laissé partir les Israélites, et les Israélites ont quitté l’Égypte.

vi.L: Sao các ông lại làm cho lòng mình cứng cỏi như người Ai Cập và Pha-ra-ôn đã làm cho lòng họ cứng cỏi? Chẳng phải khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã đối xử khắc nghiệt với họ, thì họ mới để dân ấy đi, và dân ấy đã ra đi sao?
vi.B: Sao các ông lại cứng lòng như người Ai Cập và Pha-ra-ôn đã cứng lòng? Khi vị thần ấy đã đối xử khắc nghiệt với họ, chẳng phải họ đã để dân Y-sơ-ra-ên đi, và dân ấy đã ra đi sao?
vi.R: Đừng cứng đầu như người Ai Cập và Pha-ra-ôn. Sau khi Đức Chúa Trời trừng phạt họ nặng nề, họ đã để dân Y-sơ-ra-ên đi, và dân Y-sơ-ra-ên đã rời khỏi Ai Cập.

decisions.choice: make your heart heavy: refuse to give in, as Pharaoh did
decisions.reason: The words recall the plagues in Egypt, where Pharaoh made his heart heavy and would not let Israel go (Exodus 8:11, 28; 9:34). The Philistines already knew that this God had struck Egypt (4:8). "Heavy" also ties in with the heavy hand of God (5:6, 11) and the glory of verse 5.

decisions.choice: dealt harshly: made sport of them, made them look foolish by his power
decisions.reason: The same verb is used when Yahweh tells how he dealt with Egypt (Exodus 10:2). It means to act against someone at will, showing them up as powerless.

decisions.choice: they sent them away, and they went: the Egyptians let the Israelites go
decisions.reason: The first "they" is the Egyptians and the second "them" is Israel, as in the Exodus story (Exodus 12:31-33).

decisions.choice: the Israelites
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the Israelites so that the pronouns are clear. Readable also gives "God" for "he" and turns the speaker's questions into plain statements, which say the same thing.

decisions.choice: "endurcir votre cœur"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "make your heart heavy", the words used of Pharaoh in Exodus (m1). French "endurcir le cœur" is the established phrase for Pharaoh's refusal and says what the Hebrew means; "appesantir" is understood only by those who know the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: "làm cho lòng mình cứng cỏi" (L); "cứng lòng" (B); "cứng đầu" (R) for "make your heart heavy"
decisions.reason: Refusing to give in, as Pharaoh did (meaning decision); "cứng lòng" is the Vietnamese idiom for that stubbornness, and Readable uses the everyday "cứng đầu".

source.text: וְעַתָּ֗ה קְח֨וּ וַעֲשׂ֜וּ עֲגָלָ֤ה חֲדָשָׁה֙ אֶחָ֔ת וּשְׁתֵּ֤י פָרוֹת֙ עָל֔וֹת אֲשֶׁ֛ר לֹא־עָלָ֥ה עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם עֹ֑ל וַאֲסַרְתֶּ֤ם אֶת־הַפָּרוֹת֙ בָּעֲגָלָ֔ה וַהֲשֵׁיבֹתֶ֧ם בְּנֵיהֶ֛ם מֵאַחֲרֵיהֶ֖ם הַבָּֽיְתָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And now take and make one new cart and two nursing cows on which not has come up a yoke, and harness the cows to the cart, and take back their young from after them home.

en.L: And now take and prepare one new cart and two nursing cows on which no yoke has come, and harness the cows to the cart, and take their calves back home from behind them.
en.B: Now then, get a new cart ready, and two cows that are nursing calves and have never been yoked. Harness the cows to the cart, but take their calves away from them and back home.
en.R: So get a new cart ready. Find two cows that are nursing calves and have never pulled a load. Hitch the cows to the cart, but take their calves home, away from their mothers.

es.L: Y ahora {{plural_you:tomen|tomad}} y {{plural_you:preparen|preparad}} una carreta nueva y dos vacas que estén criando, sobre las cuales no haya subido yugo, y {{plural_you:unzan|uncid}} las vacas a la carreta, y {{plural_you:lleven|llevad}} sus becerros de detrás de ellas a casa.
es.B: Ahora, pues, {{plural_you:preparen|preparad}} una carreta nueva y dos vacas que estén criando y que nunca hayan llevado yugo. {{plural_you:Unzan|Uncid}} las vacas a la carreta, pero {{plural_you:quítenles|quitadles}} los becerros y {{plural_you:llévenlos|llevadlos}} a casa.
es.R: Así que {{plural_you:preparen|preparad}} una carreta nueva. {{plural_you:Busquen|Buscad}} dos vacas que estén criando y que nunca hayan tirado de una carga. {{plural_you:Engánchenlas|Enganchadlas}} a la carreta, pero {{plural_you:lleven|llevad}} los becerros a casa, lejos de sus madres.

fr.L: Et maintenant, prenez et préparez un chariot neuf et deux vaches qui allaitent, sur lesquelles le joug n’est pas venu, et attelez les vaches au chariot, et ramenez à la maison leurs petits, loin d’elles.
fr.B: Maintenant donc, préparez un chariot neuf et deux vaches qui allaitent et qui n’ont jamais porté le joug. Attelez les vaches au chariot, mais ramenez leurs veaux à l’étable, loin d’elles.
fr.R: Alors, préparez un chariot neuf. Trouvez deux vaches qui allaitent leurs veaux et qui n’ont jamais tiré de charge. Attelez les vaches au chariot, mais ramenez leurs veaux à la maison, loin de leurs mères.

vi.L: Vậy bây giờ hãy lấy và làm một cỗ xe mới, và hai con bò cái đang cho con bú chưa hề mang ách; hãy thắng hai con bò cái vào xe, còn bê con của chúng thì đem về nhà, xa khỏi chúng.
vi.B: Vậy bây giờ hãy chuẩn bị một cỗ xe mới và hai con bò cái đang nuôi con, chưa hề mang ách. Hãy thắng hai bò cái vào xe, nhưng đem bê con của chúng về nhà.
vi.R: Vậy hãy chuẩn bị một cỗ xe mới. Hãy tìm hai con bò cái đang nuôi con và chưa hề kéo xe. Hãy thắng hai bò mẹ vào xe, còn bê con thì đem về nhà, xa bò mẹ.

decisions.choice: a new cart and cows never yoked: things not used before, fit for a holy purpose
decisions.reason: Animals that had never borne a yoke were set apart for special rites in Israel (Numbers 19:2; Deuteronomy 21:3). Unused things were fitting for carrying the ark.

decisions.choice: nursing cows whose calves are taken away: cows that will naturally want to go back to their calves
decisions.reason: Cows that had never been yoked would not pull together well, and cows separated from their calves would turn back toward them. If they went straight away from home instead, it would be a sign (verse 9).

decisions.choice: never pulled a load
decisions.reason: Readable explains being yoked by what it means for the cows.

source.text: וּלְקַחְתֶּ֞ם אֶת־אֲר֣וֹן יְהוָ֗ה וּנְתַתֶּ֤ם אֹתוֹ֙ אֶל־הָ֣עֲגָלָ֔ה וְאֵ֣ת׀כְּלֵ֣י הַזָּהָ֗ב אֲשֶׁ֨ר הֲשֵׁבֹתֶ֥ם לוֹ֙ אָשָׁ֔ם תָּשִׂ֥ימוּ בָאַרְגַּ֖ז מִצִּדּ֑וֹ וְשִׁלַּחְתֶּ֥ם אֹת֖וֹ וְהָלָֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And take [the] ark of Yahweh and put it on the cart, and the articles of gold which you are returning to him [as] a guilt offering put in a box at its side; and send it away, and it will go.

en.L: And take the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and put it on the cart, and the articles of gold that you are returning to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} [as] a guilt offering, put [them] in a box at its side. And send it away, and it will go.
en.B: Take the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and set it on the cart, and put the gold objects that you are returning to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} as a guilt offering in a box beside it. Then send it off and let it go its way.
en.R: Put the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} on the cart. Put the gold objects in a box beside it. They are your guilt offering to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Then send the cart off and let it go on its own.

es.L: Y {{plural_you:tomen|tomad}} el arca {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} y {{plural_you:pónganla|ponedla}} sobre la carreta, y los objetos de oro que {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} {{plural_you:devuelven|devolvéis}} [como] ofrenda por la culpa, {{plural_you:pónganlos|ponedlos}} en una caja a su lado. Y {{plural_you:déjenla|dejadla}} ir, y se irá.
es.B: {{plural_you:Tomen|Tomad}} el arca {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} y {{plural_you:colóquenla|colocadla}} sobre la carreta, y {{plural_you:pongan|poned}} en una caja, a su lado, los objetos de oro que {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} {{plural_you:devuelven|devolvéis}} como ofrenda por la culpa. Luego {{plural_you:déjenla|dejadla}} partir y que siga su camino.
es.R: {{plural_you:Pongan|Poned}} el arca {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} sobre la carreta. {{plural_you:Pongan|Poned}} los objetos de oro en una caja junto a ella. Son {{plural_you:su ofrenda|vuestra ofrenda}} por la culpa para {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. Luego {{plural_you:dejen|dejad}} que la carreta se vaya sola.

fr.L: Et prenez l’arche {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} et mettez-la sur le chariot ; et les objets d’or que vous {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} rendez [comme] sacrifice de réparation, mettez-[les] dans un coffret à son côté. Et renvoyez-la, et elle s’en ira.
fr.B: Prenez l’arche {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} et placez-la sur le chariot ; mettez à côté d’elle, dans un coffret, les objets d’or que vous {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} rendez comme sacrifice de réparation. Puis laissez-la partir, et qu’elle s’en aille.
fr.R: Mettez l’arche {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} sur le chariot. Mettez les objets en or dans un coffret, à côté d’elle. C’est votre offrande de réparation pour {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. Puis laissez le chariot partir tout seul.

vi.L: Hãy lấy hòm của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đặt lên xe, còn các vật bằng vàng mà các ông trả lại cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} [làm] lễ vật chuộc lỗi thì đặt [chúng] trong một cái rương bên cạnh hòm. Rồi hãy cho xe đi, và nó sẽ đi.
vi.B: Hãy lấy hòm của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đặt lên xe, và bỏ các vật bằng vàng mà các ông trả lại cho vị thần ấy làm lễ vật chuộc lỗi vào một cái rương bên cạnh. Rồi hãy cho xe đi theo đường của nó.
vi.R: Hãy đặt hòm của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} lên xe. Hãy bỏ các vật bằng vàng vào một cái rương bên cạnh hòm. Đó là lễ vật chuộc lỗi của các ông dâng cho vị thần ấy. Rồi hãy cho xe tự đi.

decisions.choice: box: a chest or case for carrying valuables
decisions.reason: The word is found only in this chapter (verses 8, 11, 15). It names a container set beside the ark, not inside it.

decisions.choice: send it away, and it will go: let it go with no one driving it
decisions.reason: No driver goes with the cart. Where it goes is left to the cows, which is the point of the test in verse 9.

decisions.choice: three short sentences
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the long instruction into steps and says "the cart" so it is clear what is sent off.

decisions.choice: "cái rương" for the box
decisions.reason: A chest for valuables (meaning decision); "rương" keeps it apart from "hòm", the ark.

source.text: וּרְאִיתֶ֗ם אִם־דֶּ֨רֶךְ גְּבוּל֤וֹ יַֽעֲלֶה֙ בֵּ֣ית שֶׁ֔מֶשׁ ה֚וּא עָ֣שָׂה לָ֔נוּ אֶת־הָרָעָ֥ה הַגְּדוֹלָ֖ה הַזֹּ֑את וְאִם־לֹ֗א וְיָדַ֨עְנוּ֙ כִּ֣י לֹ֤א יָדוֹ֙ נָ֣גְעָה בָּ֔נוּ מִקְרֶ֥ה ה֖וּא הָ֥יָה לָֽנוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And see: if [the] way of its territory it goes up, Beth-shemesh, he has done to us this great evil; and if not, then we will know that not his hand touched us; chance it [was that] happened to us.

en.L: And watch: if it goes up by the way of its own territory, [to] Beth-shemesh, [then] {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has done to us this great evil. But if not, then we will know that [it was] not {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand [that] struck us; it [was] chance [that] happened to us."
en.B: Then watch. If it goes up the road to its own territory, toward Beth-shemesh, then it is {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} who has brought this great disaster on us. But if not, we will know that it was not {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand that struck us. It just happened to us by chance."
en.R: Then watch it. If it goes up the road toward Beth-shemesh, back to the ark's own land, then the God of Israel is the one who brought this terrible trouble on us. But if it goes some other way, then we will know that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was not the one who struck us. It was only something that happened by chance."

es.L: Y {{plural_you:observen|observad}}: si sube por el camino de su propio territorio, [hacia] Bet-semes, [entonces] {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} nos ha hecho este gran mal. Pero si no, sabremos que no [fue] {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} mano [la que] nos hirió; fue una casualidad [lo que] nos sucedió».
es.B: Luego {{plural_you:observen|observad}}. Si sube por el camino de su propio territorio, hacia Bet-semes, entonces es {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} quien nos ha traído esta gran desgracia. Pero si no, sabremos que no fue {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} mano la que nos hirió. Nos sucedió por casualidad».
es.R: Luego {{plural_you:vigílenla|vigiladla}}. Si sube por el camino hacia Bet-semes, de vuelta a la tierra del arca, entonces es el Dios de Israel quien nos ha traído esta terrible desgracia. Pero si se va por otro camino, sabremos que no fue {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} quien nos hirió. Fue solo algo que pasó por casualidad».

fr.L: Et regardez : si elle monte par le chemin de son territoire, [vers] Beth-Shémesh, [c’est] {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} [qui] nous a fait ce grand mal. Mais sinon, nous saurons que [ce n’est] pas {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} main [qui] nous a frappés ; c’[est] un hasard [qui] nous est arrivé. »
fr.B: Ensuite, observez. Si elle monte par la route de son propre territoire, vers Beth-Shémesh, c’est {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} qui nous a causé ce grand malheur. Sinon, nous saurons que ce n’est pas {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} main qui nous a frappés. Ce qui nous est arrivé n’était qu’un hasard. »
fr.R: Ensuite, regardez bien. Si le chariot prend la route de Beth-Shémesh, vers le pays de l’arche, alors c’est le Dieu d’Israël qui nous a causé ce terrible malheur. Mais s’il part dans une autre direction, nous saurons que ce n’est pas {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} qui nous a frappés. C’était seulement un hasard. »

vi.L: Hãy xem: nếu nó đi lên theo đường về lãnh thổ của nó, [về] Bết-Sê-mết, [thì] chính {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã giáng tai họa lớn này trên chúng ta. Còn nếu không, thì chúng ta sẽ biết rằng không phải tay {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã đánh chúng ta; [ấy là] chuyện ngẫu nhiên đã xảy đến cho chúng ta."
vi.B: Rồi hãy theo dõi. Nếu xe đi lên con đường về lãnh thổ của nó, hướng về Bết-Sê-mết, thì chính vị thần ấy đã giáng tai họa lớn này trên chúng ta. Còn nếu không, chúng ta sẽ biết rằng không phải tay vị thần ấy đã đánh chúng ta. Đó chỉ là chuyện tình cờ xảy đến cho chúng ta thôi."
vi.R: Rồi hãy theo dõi. Nếu xe đi lên đường về hướng Bết-Sê-mết, trở về xứ của hòm, thì chính Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên đã giáng tai họa khủng khiếp này trên chúng ta. Nhưng nếu xe đi hướng khác, thì chúng ta sẽ biết không phải vị thần ấy đã đánh chúng ta. Đó chỉ là chuyện tình cờ mà thôi."

decisions.choice: Beth-shemesh: an Israelite town on the border nearest Philistine land
decisions.reason: Beth-shemesh lay in the valley of Sorek, the first Israelite town on the road from Ekron, and it was one of the towns given to the priests (Joshua 15:10; 21:16).

decisions.choice: he has done: he himself, the God of Israel, is the one who did it
decisions.reason: The Hebrew adds the pronoun for emphasis. The test is meant to show whether this God, and no other cause, brought the plague.

decisions.choice: evil: disaster, harm
decisions.reason: The word here means harm suffered, not wrongdoing.

decisions.choice: chance: something that simply happens, with no one causing it
decisions.reason: The same word is used of Ruth "happening" to come to Boaz's field (Ruth 2:3). The diviners leave room for the plague to have been bad luck.

decisions.choice: back to the ark's own land; the God of Israel
decisions.reason: Readable says whose territory is meant and names the God of Israel for the emphatic "he".

decisions.choice: "Beth-Shémesh"
decisions.reason: The usual French form of the name ("house of the sun"), with the accent French writes on the e; used through 1 Samuel.

decisions.choice: "Bet-semes"; "Quiriat-jearim" (verse 21)
decisions.reason: Names in their usual Spanish form, as the Samuel terms note gives "Quiriat-jearim"; kept the same through both books.

decisions.choice: "Bết-Sê-mết"
decisions.reason: The usual Protestant transliteration; kept through the book, with "người Bết-Sê-mết" for "the Beth-shemeshite" (verse 14).

source.text: וַיַּעֲשׂ֤וּ הָאֲנָשִׁים֙ כֵּ֔ן וַיִּקְח֗וּ שְׁתֵּ֤י פָרוֹת֙ עָל֔וֹת וַיַּאַסְר֖וּם בָּעֲגָלָ֑ה וְאֶת־בְּנֵיהֶ֖ם כָּל֥וּ בַבָּֽיִת׃

records.literal_gloss: And did the men so, and they took two nursing cows and harnessed them to the cart, and their young they shut up at home.

en.L: And the men did so, and they took two nursing cows and harnessed them to the cart, and their calves they shut up at home.
en.B: The men did this. They took two cows that were nursing calves and harnessed them to the cart, and they penned up their calves at home.
en.R: The men did what they were told. They took two mother cows and hitched them to the cart. They kept the calves shut up at home.

es.L: Y los hombres lo hicieron así, y tomaron dos vacas que estaban criando y las uncieron a la carreta, y encerraron en casa a sus becerros.
es.B: Los hombres así lo hicieron. Tomaron dos vacas que estaban criando y las uncieron a la carreta, y encerraron a sus becerros en casa.
es.R: Los hombres hicieron lo que se les dijo. Tomaron dos vacas que estaban criando y las engancharon a la carreta. A los becerros los dejaron encerrados en casa.

fr.L: Et les hommes firent ainsi : ils prirent deux vaches qui allaitaient et les attelèrent au chariot, et ils enfermèrent leurs petits à la maison.
fr.B: Les hommes firent ainsi. Ils prirent deux vaches qui allaitaient, les attelèrent au chariot et enfermèrent leurs veaux à l’étable.
fr.R: Les hommes ont fait ce qu’on leur avait dit. Ils ont pris deux vaches qui avaient des veaux et les ont attelées au chariot. Ils ont gardé les veaux enfermés à la maison.

vi.L: Những người ấy làm như vậy: họ bắt hai con bò cái đang cho con bú thắng vào xe, còn bê con của chúng thì nhốt ở nhà.
vi.B: Người ta làm đúng như vậy. Họ bắt hai con bò cái đang nuôi con thắng vào xe, và nhốt bê con của chúng ở nhà.
vi.R: Người ta làm đúng như lời được dặn. Họ bắt hai con bò mẹ thắng vào xe. Họ nhốt bê con ở nhà.

decisions.choice: the men did so: the Philistines followed the advice exactly
decisions.reason: Each step of verses 7-8 is carried out in verses 10-11.

decisions.choice: mother cows
decisions.reason: Readable says "mother cows" for cows nursing calves, as in verse 7.

source.text: וַיָּשִׂ֛מוּ אֶת־אֲר֥וֹן יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־הָעֲגָלָ֑ה וְאֵ֣ת הָאַרְגַּ֗ז וְאֵת֙ עַכְבְּרֵ֣י הַזָּהָ֔ב וְאֵ֖ת צַלְמֵ֥י טְחֹרֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And they put [the] ark of Yahweh on the cart, and the box, and the mice of gold, and the images of their tumors.

en.L: And they put the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} on the cart, and the box, and the rats of gold, and the images of their tumors.
en.B: They set the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} on the cart, along with the box, the gold rats and the images of their tumors.
en.R: They put the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} on the cart. They also put the box on it with the gold rats and the gold models of their tumors.

es.L: Y pusieron el arca {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} sobre la carreta, y la caja, y las ratas de oro, y las imágenes de sus tumores.
es.B: Colocaron el arca {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} sobre la carreta, junto con la caja, las ratas de oro y las imágenes de sus tumores.
es.R: Pusieron el arca {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} sobre la carreta. También pusieron en ella la caja con las ratas de oro y las figuras de oro de sus tumores.

fr.L: Et ils mirent l’arche {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} sur le chariot, et le coffret, et les rats d’or, et les images de leurs tumeurs.
fr.B: Ils placèrent l’arche {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} sur le chariot, avec le coffret, les rats d’or et les images de leurs tumeurs.
fr.R: Ils ont mis l’arche {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} sur le chariot. Ils y ont mis aussi le coffret, avec les rats en or et les modèles en or de leurs tumeurs.

vi.L: Họ đặt hòm của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} lên xe, cùng với cái rương, các con chuột bằng vàng và các hình bướu của họ.
vi.B: Họ đặt hòm của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} lên xe, cùng với cái rương đựng các con chuột bằng vàng và các hình bướu của họ.
vi.R: Họ đặt hòm của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} lên xe. Họ cũng đặt lên xe cái rương có các con chuột bằng vàng và các mô hình bướu bằng vàng.

decisions.choice: the box and the gold rats and images: the box holding the gold offering
decisions.reason: Verse 8 told them to put the gold objects in the box, so the list names the box together with what was in it.

decisions.choice: the box ... with; gold models
decisions.reason: Readable shows that the gold objects were in the box, and says they were gold as verse 4 does.

source.text: וַיִשַּׁ֨רְנָההַפָּר֜וֹת בַּדֶּ֗רֶךְ עַל־דֶּ֨רֶךְ֙ בֵּ֣ית שֶׁ֔מֶשׁ בִּמְסִלָּ֣ה אַחַ֗ת הָלְכ֤וּ הָלֹךְ֙ וְגָע֔וֹ וְלֹא־סָ֖רוּ יָמִ֣ין וּשְׂמֹ֑אול וְסַרְנֵ֤י פְלִשְׁתִּים֙ הֹלְכִ֣ים אַחֲרֵיהֶ֔ם עַד־גְּב֖וּל בֵּ֥ית שָֽׁמֶשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: And went straight the cows on the way, on [the] way of Beth-shemesh; on one highway they went, going and lowing, and not they turned aside right or left; and [the] rulers of [the] Philistines [were] walking after them as far as [the] border of Beth-shemesh.

en.L: And the cows went straight on the road, on the road to Beth-shemesh. On one highway they went, lowing as they went, and they did not turn aside [to the] right or [to the] left. And the rulers of [the] Philistines [were] walking behind them as far as the border of Beth-shemesh.
en.B: The cows went straight along the road toward Beth-shemesh. They kept to the one highway, lowing as they went, and did not turn to the right or the left. The rulers of the Philistines walked behind them as far as the border of Beth-shemesh.
en.R: The cows headed straight for Beth-shemesh. They stayed on the main road, mooing all the way, and did not turn off to either side. The Philistine rulers followed them as far as the edge of Beth-shemesh.

es.L: Y las vacas fueron derecho por el camino, por el camino de Bet-semes. Por una sola calzada iban, mugiendo mientras andaban, y no se desviaron [a la] derecha ni [a la] izquierda. Y los jefes de [los] filisteos iban caminando detrás de ellas hasta el límite de Bet-semes.
es.B: Las vacas siguieron derecho por el camino hacia Bet-semes. Fueron siempre por la misma calzada, mugiendo mientras andaban, sin desviarse ni a la derecha ni a la izquierda. Los jefes de los filisteos fueron caminando detrás de ellas hasta el límite de Bet-semes.
es.R: Las vacas se fueron directo hacia Bet-semes. Siguieron por el camino principal, mugiendo todo el tiempo, y no se apartaron hacia ningún lado. Los jefes filisteos las siguieron hasta la entrada de Bet-semes.

fr.L: Et les vaches allèrent droit par le chemin, sur le chemin de Beth-Shémesh ; elles allèrent par une seule route, allant et mugissant, et elles ne s’écartèrent ni à droite ni à gauche. Et les princes des Philistins marchaient derrière elles jusqu’à la frontière de Beth-Shémesh.
fr.B: Les vaches prirent tout droit la route de Beth-Shémesh. Elles suivirent la même route en mugissant, sans s’écarter ni à droite ni à gauche. Les princes des Philistins marchèrent derrière elles jusqu’à la frontière de Beth-Shémesh.
fr.R: Les vaches sont allées tout droit vers Beth-Shémesh. Elles sont restées sur la grande route, en meuglant tout le long du chemin, et elles n’ont tourné ni d’un côté ni de l’autre. Les princes des Philistins les ont suivies jusqu’à l’entrée du territoire de Beth-Shémesh.

vi.L: Hai con bò cái đi thẳng trên đường, trên đường về Bết-Sê-mết. Chúng cứ đi trên một con đường cái, vừa đi vừa rống, không rẽ sang [bên] phải hay [bên] trái. Các lãnh chúa Phi-li-tin đi theo sau chúng cho đến ranh giới Bết-Sê-mết.
vi.B: Hai con bò cái đi thẳng theo đường về Bết-Sê-mết. Chúng cứ đi trên con đường cái, vừa đi vừa rống, không rẽ sang phải hay trái. Các lãnh chúa Phi-li-tin đi theo sau cho đến ranh giới Bết-Sê-mết.
vi.R: Hai con bò đi thẳng về hướng Bết-Sê-mết. Chúng cứ theo đường cái mà đi, vừa đi vừa rống, không hề rẽ sang bên nào. Các lãnh chúa Phi-li-tin đi theo chúng đến tận ranh giới Bết-Sê-mết.

decisions.choice: the cows went straight: the sign of verse 9 is given
decisions.reason: Cows that had never been yoked, taken from their calves, would be expected to wander or turn back home. They went straight to Israel's border, showing that the God of Israel had sent the plague and was bringing his ark home.

decisions.choice: lowing as they went: crying out for their calves
decisions.reason: The cows called for their calves the whole way and yet did not turn back to them, which makes the sign stronger.

decisions.choice: the rulers walked behind: they watched the test themselves
decisions.reason: The five rulers followed to see the outcome with their own eyes, and stopped at the border of Israelite land.

decisions.choice: mooing; did not turn off to either side
decisions.reason: Readable uses the everyday word for a cow's call and says "to either side" for "right or left".

source.text: וּבֵ֣ית שֶׁ֔מֶשׁ קֹצְרִ֥ים קְצִיר־חִטִּ֖ים בָּעֵ֑מֶק וַיִּשְׂא֣וּ אֶת־עֵינֵיהֶ֗ם וַיִּרְאוּ֙ אֶת־הָ֣אָר֔וֹן וַֽיִּשְׂמְח֖וּ לִרְאֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And Beth-shemesh [were] reaping [the] harvest of wheat in the valley, and they lifted their eyes and saw the ark, and they rejoiced to see [it].

en.L: And [the people of] Beth-shemesh [were] reaping [the] wheat harvest in the valley, and they lifted up their eyes and saw the ark, and they rejoiced to see [it].
en.B: Now the people of Beth-shemesh were out in the valley reaping the wheat harvest. When they looked up and saw the ark, they were glad at the sight.
en.R: The people of Beth-shemesh were cutting their wheat in the valley. They looked up and saw the ark, and they were full of joy to see it.

es.L: Y [los de] Bet-semes [estaban] segando [la] cosecha del trigo en el valle, y alzaron sus ojos y vieron el arca, y se alegraron al ver[la].
es.B: Los habitantes de Bet-semes estaban en el valle segando el trigo. Cuando alzaron la vista y vieron el arca, se alegraron al verla.
es.R: La gente de Bet-semes estaba cortando su trigo en el valle. Levantaron la vista y vieron el arca, y se llenaron de alegría al verla.

fr.L: Et [les gens de] Beth-Shémesh moissonnaient le blé dans la vallée ; et ils levèrent les yeux et virent l’arche, et ils se réjouirent de [la] voir.
fr.B: Les habitants de Beth-Shémesh étaient en train de moissonner le blé dans la vallée. Levant les yeux, ils aperçurent l’arche et se réjouirent de la voir.
fr.R: Les habitants de Beth-Shémesh coupaient leur blé dans la vallée. Ils ont levé les yeux et ont vu l’arche. Ils ont été remplis de joie en la voyant.

vi.L: [Dân] Bết-Sê-mết [đang] gặt lúa mì trong thung lũng; họ ngước mắt lên thấy hòm, và họ vui mừng khi thấy [hòm].
vi.B: Bấy giờ dân Bết-Sê-mết đang gặt lúa mì trong thung lũng. Khi ngước mắt lên thấy hòm, họ vui mừng khôn xiết.
vi.R: Dân Bết-Sê-mết đang gặt lúa mì trong thung lũng. Họ ngước lên và thấy hòm, và họ rất vui mừng.

decisions.choice: Beth-shemesh: the people of the town
decisions.reason: The town's name stands for the people who lived there, and the verbs that follow are plural.

decisions.choice: the wheat harvest: late spring, around May and June
decisions.reason: Wheat was harvested after barley, in the weeks before the Festival of Weeks (Exodus 34:22). The townspeople were out in the fields of the valley below the town.

decisions.choice: lifted up their eyes: looked up
decisions.reason: The phrase means to look up and notice something, often with surprise (Genesis 22:4).

decisions.choice: the people of Beth-shemesh
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who was reaping.

source.text: וְהָעֲגָלָ֡ה בָּ֠אָה אֶל־שְׂדֵ֨ה יְהוֹשֻׁ֤עַ בֵּֽית־הַשִּׁמְשִׁי֙ וַתַּעֲמֹ֣ד שָׁ֔ם וְשָׁ֖ם אֶ֣בֶן גְּדוֹלָ֑ה וַֽיְבַקְּעוּ֙ אֶת־עֲצֵ֣י הָעֲגָלָ֔ה וְאֶת־הַ֨פָּר֔וֹת הֶעֱל֥וּ עֹלָ֖ה לַיהוָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And the cart came to [the] field of Joshua the Beth-shemeshite and stood there, and there [was] a large stone; and they split the wood of the cart, and the cows they offered up [as] a burnt offering to Yahweh.

en.L: And the cart came to the field of Joshua the Beth-shemeshite and stopped there, and there [was] a large stone there. And they split the wood of the cart, and they offered up the cows [as] a burnt offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: The cart reached the field of Joshua of Beth-shemesh and stopped there, where there was a large stone. The people split up the cart's wood and sacrificed the cows to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as a burnt offering.
en.R: The cart came into a field that belonged to a man named Joshua from Beth-shemesh. It stopped there, where there was a large rock. The people broke up the cart for firewood and offered the cows as a burnt offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

es.L: Y la carreta llegó al campo de Josué el de Bet-semes y se detuvo allí, y allí [había] una piedra grande. Y partieron la madera de la carreta, y ofrecieron las vacas [en] holocausto {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}.
es.B: La carreta llegó al campo de Josué de Bet-semes y se detuvo allí, donde había una piedra grande. La gente partió la madera de la carreta y ofreció las vacas {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} en holocausto.
es.R: La carreta entró en un campo que era de un hombre llamado Josué, de Bet-semes. Se detuvo allí, donde había una roca grande. La gente hizo leña con la carreta y ofreció las vacas como holocausto {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}.

fr.L: Et le chariot arriva au champ de Josué le Beth-Shémite et s’arrêta là ; et il y [avait] là une grande pierre. Et ils fendirent le bois du chariot, et ils offrirent les vaches en holocauste {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Le chariot arriva dans le champ de Josué de Beth-Shémesh et s’arrêta là, près d’une grande pierre. On fendit le bois du chariot, et l’on offrit les vaches en holocauste {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Le chariot est entré dans le champ d’un homme appelé Josué, de Beth-Shémesh. Il s’est arrêté là, près d’un gros rocher. Les gens ont cassé le chariot pour faire du bois et ont offert les vaches {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} en sacrifice complet par le feu.

vi.L: Xe đến cánh đồng của Giô-suê người Bết-Sê-mết và dừng lại đó; ở đó có một tảng đá lớn. Họ chẻ gỗ của xe và dâng hai con bò cái [làm] tế lễ thiêu cho {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.
vi.B: Xe đến cánh đồng của Giô-suê, người Bết-Sê-mết, và dừng lại đó, nơi có một tảng đá lớn. Dân chúng chẻ gỗ xe ra và dâng hai con bò cái làm tế lễ thiêu cho {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.
vi.R: Xe đi vào cánh đồng của một người tên là Giô-suê ở Bết-Sê-mết. Xe dừng lại ở đó, nơi có một tảng đá lớn. Dân chúng chẻ xe ra làm củi và dâng hai con bò làm tế lễ thiêu cho {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.

decisions.choice: Joshua the Beth-shemeshite: a landowner of the town, not Joshua son of Nun
decisions.reason: He is named only here and in verse 18. Naming the owner of the field tells the first readers where the stone could be found.

decisions.choice: the cart and the cows offered: what had carried the ark was not put back to common use
decisions.reason: The cart and cows had served a holy purpose, so the people burned them as an offering to Yahweh. Leviticus 1:3 asks for a male animal for a burnt offering, but the story does not stop to comment on that.

decisions.choice: they split ... they offered: the people of Beth-shemesh
decisions.reason: The subject is not named; the people who had run to see the ark (verse 13) are meant. Verse 15 adds that Levites took the ark down.

decisions.choice: the people
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the subject. Readable says the cart was broken up "for firewood" because that is why its wood was split.

decisions.choice: "en sacrifice complet par le feu"
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced say "holocauste", the term of the Pentateuch note. In today's French the word also names the Shoah, so Readable says what the offering was, an animal burned whole on the altar, as the English Readable does with "burnt offering".

decisions.choice: "Giô-suê"
decisions.reason: The same Hebrew name as Joshua son of Nun, in the form of the Vietnamese New Testament (Acts 7:45); the meaning decision says it is another man.

source.text: וְהַלְוִיִּ֞ם הוֹרִ֣ידוּ׀אֶת־אֲר֣וֹן יְהוָ֗ה וְאֶת־הָאַרְגַּ֤ז אֲשֶׁר־אִתּוֹ֙ אֲשֶׁר־בּ֣וֹ כְלֵֽי־זָהָ֔ב וַיָּשִׂ֖מוּ אֶל־הָאֶ֣בֶן הַגְּדוֹלָ֑ה וְאַנְשֵׁ֣י בֵֽית־שֶׁ֗מֶשׁ הֶעֱל֨וּ עֹל֜וֹת וַֽיִּזְבְּח֧וּ זְבָחִ֛ים בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא לַֽיהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And the Levites brought down [the] ark of Yahweh and the box which [was] with it, which in it [were the] articles of gold, and they put [them] on the large stone; and [the] men of Beth-shemesh offered up burnt offerings and sacrificed sacrifices on that day to Yahweh.

en.L: And the Levites took down the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and the box that [was] with it, in which [were the] articles of gold, and they put [them] on the large stone. And the men of Beth-shemesh offered up burnt offerings and sacrificed sacrifices on that day to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: The Levites had taken down the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and the box with it that held the gold objects, and had set them on the large stone. On that day the men of Beth-shemesh brought burnt offerings and other sacrifices to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: The Levites had already lifted down the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and the box with the gold objects in it. They had set them on the large rock. That same day the men of Beth-shemesh gave burnt offerings and other sacrifices to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

es.L: Y los levitas bajaron el arca {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} y la caja que [estaba] con ella, en la cual [estaban] los objetos de oro, y [los] pusieron sobre la piedra grande. Y los hombres de Bet-semes ofrecieron holocaustos y sacrificaron sacrificios aquel día {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}.
es.B: Los levitas habían bajado el arca {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} y la caja que estaba con ella, donde iban los objetos de oro, y los habían puesto sobre la piedra grande. Aquel día los hombres de Bet-semes ofrecieron holocaustos y otros sacrificios {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}.
es.R: Los levitas ya habían bajado el arca {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} y la caja con los objetos de oro. Los habían puesto sobre la roca grande. Ese mismo día, los hombres de Bet-semes presentaron holocaustos y otros sacrificios {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}.

fr.L: Et les Lévites descendirent l’arche {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} et le coffret qui [était] avec elle, dans lequel [étaient] les objets d’or, et ils [les] mirent sur la grande pierre. Et les hommes de Beth-Shémesh offrirent des holocaustes et sacrifièrent des sacrifices ce jour-là {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Les Lévites avaient descendu l’arche {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} ainsi que le coffret qui l’accompagnait et qui contenait les objets d’or, et ils les avaient posés sur la grande pierre. Ce jour-là, les hommes de Beth-Shémesh offrirent {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} des holocaustes et d’autres sacrifices.
fr.R: Les Lévites avaient déjà descendu l’arche {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} et le coffret qui contenait les objets en or. Ils les avaient posés sur le gros rocher. Ce jour-là, les hommes de Beth-Shémesh ont offert {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} des sacrifices complets par le feu et d’autres sacrifices.

vi.L: Người Lê-vi khiêng hòm của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} xuống, cùng cái rương ở bên hòm, trong đó [có] các vật bằng vàng, và đặt [chúng] trên tảng đá lớn. Trong ngày ấy, người Bết-Sê-mết dâng các tế lễ thiêu và dâng các sinh tế cho {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.
vi.B: Người Lê-vi đã khiêng hòm của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} xuống, cùng cái rương bên cạnh đựng các vật bằng vàng, và đặt trên tảng đá lớn. Ngày ấy người Bết-Sê-mết dâng tế lễ thiêu và các sinh tế khác cho {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.
vi.R: Người Lê-vi đã khiêng hòm của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} xuống, cùng với cái rương đựng các vật bằng vàng. Họ đặt chúng trên tảng đá lớn. Ngay ngày hôm ấy, người Bết-Sê-mết dâng tế lễ thiêu và các sinh tế khác cho {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.

decisions.choice: the Levites: the tribe set apart to carry the ark
decisions.reason: Only the Levites were to carry the ark (Numbers 4:15; Deuteronomy 10:8). Beth-shemesh was one of the towns given to the priests of Levi's tribe (Joshua 21:16), so Levites lived there.

decisions.choice: took down: done before the cart was burned
decisions.reason: The verse goes back to say what happened to the ark before the cart was broken up and burned in verse 14. The Levites lifted it off and set it on the stone first.

decisions.choice: burnt offerings and sacrifices: offerings wholly burned and offerings shared in a meal
decisions.reason: A burnt offering was burned entirely on the altar. The other sacrifices were partly burned and partly eaten by the worshipers, as a meal of thanks (Leviticus 1; 3).

decisions.choice: had taken down; had set
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use "had" to show that this was done before the burning in verse 14.

source.text: וַחֲמִשָּׁ֥ה סַרְנֵֽי־פְלִשְׁתִּ֖ים רָא֑וּ וַיָּשֻׁ֥בוּ עֶקְר֖וֹן בַּיּ֥וֹם הַהֽוּא׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And five rulers of Philistines saw, and they returned [to] Ekron on that day.

en.L: And [the] five rulers of [the] Philistines saw [it], and they returned [to] Ekron on that day.
en.B: When the five rulers of the Philistines had seen this, they went back to Ekron that same day.
en.R: The five Philistine rulers watched all this. Then they went back to Ekron that same day.

es.L: Y [los] cinco jefes de [los] filisteos [lo] vieron, y volvieron [a] Ecrón aquel día.
es.B: Cuando los cinco jefes de los filisteos vieron esto, regresaron a Ecrón ese mismo día.
es.R: Los cinco jefes filisteos vieron todo esto. Después regresaron a Ecrón ese mismo día.

fr.L: Et les cinq princes des Philistins [le] virent, et ils retournèrent à Eqrôn ce jour-là.
fr.B: Après avoir vu cela, les cinq princes des Philistins retournèrent à Eqrôn le jour même.
fr.R: Les cinq princes des Philistins ont regardé tout cela. Puis ils sont retournés à Eqrôn le jour même.

vi.L: Năm lãnh chúa Phi-li-tin thấy [vậy], và họ trở về Éc-rôn trong ngày ấy.
vi.B: Năm lãnh chúa Phi-li-tin thấy vậy thì trở về Éc-rôn ngay trong ngày.
vi.R: Năm lãnh chúa Phi-li-tin chứng kiến mọi việc. Rồi họ trở về Éc-rôn ngay trong ngày hôm ấy.

decisions.choice: Ekron: the nearest Philistine city, where the ark had last been held
decisions.reason: The ark had been sent from Gath to Ekron, and the people of Ekron demanded that it be sent away (5:10-12). The road from Ekron ran east to Beth-shemesh.

decisions.choice: saw: saw what had happened, the cows' journey and the welcome at Beth-shemesh
decisions.reason: The verb has no object; the whole scene is meant. The rulers saw the sign for themselves.

decisions.choice: this; all this
decisions.reason: English needs an object for "saw".

source.text: וְאֵ֨לֶּה֙ טְחֹרֵ֣י הַזָּהָ֔ב אֲשֶׁ֨ר הֵשִׁ֧יבוּ פְלִשְׁתִּ֛ים אָשָׁ֖ם לַֽיהוָ֑ה לְאַשְׁדּ֨וֹד אֶחָ֜דלְעַזָּ֤ה אֶחָד֙ לְאַשְׁקְל֣וֹן אֶחָ֔ד לְגַ֥ת אֶחָ֖ד לְעֶקְר֥וֹן אֶחָֽד׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And these [are] the tumors of gold which returned [the] Philistines [as] a guilt offering to Yahweh: for Ashdod one, for Gaza one, for Ashkelon one, for Gath one, for Ekron one.

en.L: And these [are] the tumors of gold that [the] Philistines returned [as] a guilt offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: for Ashdod one, for Gaza one, for Ashkelon one, for Gath one, for Ekron one.
en.B: These are the gold tumors that the Philistines returned as a guilt offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: one for Ashdod, one for Gaza, one for Ashkelon, one for Gath and one for Ekron.
en.R: The Philistines sent back gold tumors as a guilt offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. There was one for each of their cities: Ashdod, Gaza, Ashkelon, Gath and Ekron.

es.L: Y estos [son] los tumores de oro que [los] filisteos devolvieron [como] ofrenda por la culpa {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}: por Asdod uno, por Gaza uno, por Ascalón uno, por Gat uno, por Ecrón uno.
es.B: Estos son los tumores de oro que los filisteos devolvieron {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} como ofrenda por la culpa: uno por Asdod, uno por Gaza, uno por Ascalón, uno por Gat y uno por Ecrón.
es.R: Los filisteos enviaron tumores de oro como ofrenda por la culpa {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}. Había uno por cada una de sus ciudades: Asdod, Gaza, Ascalón, Gat y Ecrón.

fr.L: Et voici les tumeurs d’or que les Philistins rendirent [comme] sacrifice de réparation {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} : pour Ashdod une, pour Gaza une, pour Ashqelôn une, pour Gath une, pour Eqrôn une.
fr.B: Voici les tumeurs d’or que les Philistins rendirent {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} comme sacrifice de réparation : une pour Ashdod, une pour Gaza, une pour Ashqelôn, une pour Gath et une pour Eqrôn.
fr.R: Les Philistins ont envoyé des tumeurs en or comme offrande de réparation {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}. Il y en avait une pour chacune de leurs villes : Ashdod, Gaza, Ashqelôn, Gath et Eqrôn.

vi.L: Đây [là] các cái bướu bằng vàng mà người Phi-li-tin đã trả lại [làm] lễ vật chuộc lỗi cho {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}: một cho Ách-đốt, một cho Ga-xa, một cho Ách-kê-lôn, một cho Gát, một cho Éc-rôn.
vi.B: Đây là các cái bướu bằng vàng mà người Phi-li-tin trả lại làm lễ vật chuộc lỗi cho {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}: một cho Ách-đốt, một cho Ga-xa, một cho Ách-kê-lôn, một cho Gát và một cho Éc-rôn.
vi.R: Người Phi-li-tin gửi trả các cái bướu bằng vàng làm lễ vật chuộc lỗi cho {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. Mỗi thành của họ có một cái: Ách-đốt, Ga-xa, Ách-kê-lôn, Gát và Éc-rôn.

decisions.choice: Ashdod, Gaza, Ashkelon, Gath, Ekron: the five Philistine cities
decisions.reason: These were the chief cities of the Philistines on the coastal plain, each with its own ruler (verse 4; Joshua 13:3). Ashdod, Gath and Ekron had held the ark (5:1-10).

decisions.choice: tumors: as in verse 4
decisions.reason: Here the written text and the reading tradition agree on the word for tumors used in verse 4.

decisions.choice: two sentences
decisions.reason: Readable turns the list into a plain sentence naming the cities.

decisions.choice: "Ga-xa", "Ách-kê-lôn"
decisions.reason: The usual Protestant forms; "Ga-xa" is also the form of the Vietnamese Acts 8:26.

source.text: וְעַכְבְּרֵ֣י הַזָּהָ֗ב מִסְפַּ֞ר כָּל־עָרֵ֤י פְלִשְׁתִּים֙ לַחֲמֵ֣שֶׁת הַסְּרָנִ֔ים מֵעִ֣יר מִבְצָ֔ר וְעַ֖ד כֹּ֣פֶר הַפְּרָזִ֑י וְעַ֣ד׀אָבֵ֣ל הַגְּדוֹלָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר הִנִּ֤יחוּ עָלֶ֨יהָ֙ אֵ֚ת אֲר֣וֹן יְהוָ֔ה עַ֚ד הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֔ה בִּשְׂדֵ֥ה יְהוֹשֻׁ֖עַ בֵּֽית־הַשִּׁמְשִֽׁי׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] mice of gold, [the] number of all [the] cities of [the] Philistines belonging to the five rulers, from city of fortification and to village of the open country; and as far as Abel the great, which they set down on it [the] ark of Yahweh, until this day, in [the] field of Joshua the Beth-shemeshite.

en.L: And the rats of gold [were by the] number of all the cities of [the] Philistines belonging to the five rulers, from fortified city to village of the open country, as far as the great stone on which they set down the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. [It is there] to this day in the field of Joshua the Beth-shemeshite.
en.B: The gold rats matched the number of all the Philistine cities belonging to the five rulers, from fortified cities to country villages, as far as the large stone on which they set the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. That stone is still there to this day in the field of Joshua of Beth-shemesh.
en.R: The gold rats stood for all the Philistine towns that belonged to the five rulers, from walled cities to country villages, all the way to the large rock where the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was set down. That rock is still in Joshua's field at Beth-shemesh to this day.

es.L: Y las ratas de oro [eran según el] número de todas las ciudades de [los] filisteos que pertenecían a los cinco jefes, desde la ciudad fortificada hasta la aldea del campo abierto, hasta la gran piedra sobre la cual pusieron el arca {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}. [Está allí] hasta el día de hoy en el campo de Josué el de Bet-semes.
es.B: Las ratas de oro correspondían al número de todas las ciudades filisteas que pertenecían a los cinco jefes, desde las ciudades fortificadas hasta las aldeas del campo, hasta la piedra grande sobre la cual pusieron el arca {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}. Esa piedra sigue allí hasta el día de hoy, en el campo de Josué de Bet-semes.
es.R: Las ratas de oro representaban a todos los pueblos filisteos que pertenecían a los cinco jefes, desde las ciudades con murallas hasta las aldeas del campo, y hasta la roca grande donde pusieron el arca {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}. Esa roca sigue hasta el día de hoy en el campo de Josué, en Bet-semes.

fr.L: Et les rats d’or [étaient selon le] nombre de toutes les villes des Philistins appartenant aux cinq princes, depuis la ville fortifiée jusqu’au village de la campagne, jusqu’à la grande pierre sur laquelle ils déposèrent l’arche {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. [Elle est là] jusqu’à ce jour, dans le champ de Josué le Beth-Shémite.
fr.B: Les rats d’or correspondaient au nombre de toutes les villes philistines qui appartenaient aux cinq princes, depuis les villes fortifiées jusqu’aux villages de la campagne, jusqu’à la grande pierre sur laquelle on déposa l’arche {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. Cette pierre est encore aujourd’hui dans le champ de Josué de Beth-Shémesh.
fr.R: Les rats en or représentaient toutes les villes des Philistins qui appartenaient aux cinq princes, depuis les villes entourées de murailles jusqu’aux villages de la campagne, jusqu’au gros rocher où l’on avait déposé l’arche {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. Ce rocher est encore aujourd’hui dans le champ de Josué, à Beth-Shémesh.

vi.L: Còn các con chuột bằng vàng [thì theo] số tất cả các thành Phi-li-tin thuộc năm lãnh chúa, từ thành kiên cố đến làng mạc ngoài đồng quê, cho đến tảng đá lớn mà trên đó họ đặt hòm của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. [Tảng đá ấy vẫn còn] cho đến ngày nay trong cánh đồng của Giô-suê người Bết-Sê-mết.
vi.B: Các con chuột bằng vàng thì theo số tất cả các thành Phi-li-tin thuộc năm lãnh chúa, từ các thành kiên cố đến các làng quê, cho đến tảng đá lớn mà họ đã đặt hòm của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} lên đó. Tảng đá ấy vẫn còn trong cánh đồng của Giô-suê người Bết-Sê-mết cho đến ngày nay.
vi.R: Các con chuột bằng vàng thì tượng trưng cho tất cả các thành Phi-li-tin thuộc năm lãnh chúa, từ các thành có tường bao quanh đến các làng quê, cho đến tận tảng đá lớn nơi hòm của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} được đặt xuống. Tảng đá ấy vẫn còn trong cánh đồng của Giô-suê ở Bết-Sê-mết cho đến ngày nay.

decisions.choice: the great stone: the stone of verses 14 and 15
alternatives: as far as the great meadow
decisions.reason: The standard Hebrew text has "Abel", a word that means "meadow" or "mourning" and is part of several place names. The two words look very much alike in Hebrew, and some Hebrew manuscripts, the ancient Greek translation and the Aramaic paraphrase read "stone", which fits the large stone already named in verses 14 and 15. The stone is followed here; if "Abel" is kept, it would be a place called "the great meadow" or a name recalling the mourning of verse 19.

decisions.choice: the gold rats ... as far as the great stone: the offering stood for the whole Philistine land, up to the border stone
alternatives: and the great stone is a witness to this day
decisions.reason: The Hebrew sentence is loosely joined. The rats stood for every Philistine town from walled city to village, and the list reaches as far as the stone on Israel's border where the ark was set down. Another way to take it is that "as far as" introduces a new statement: the great stone is a witness to this day. The ancient Greek reads it that way.

decisions.choice: the number of all the cities: more than five rats, it seems
decisions.reason: Verse 4 spoke of five gold rats, one for each ruler, while this verse links the rats to every town, large and small. The text does not explain the difference; perhaps the rats were added for the smaller towns beyond the five that the tumors stood for.

decisions.choice: to this day: until the time the account was written
decisions.reason: As at 5:5, the phrase refers to the writer's own day: his first readers could still see the stone in Joshua's field.

decisions.choice: fortified cities to country villages (Balanced); walled cities to country villages (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Village of the open country" means a village without walls (Deuteronomy 3:5), so the phrase covers every kind of town.

source.text: וַיַּ֞ךְ בְּאַנְשֵׁ֣י בֵֽית־שֶׁ֗מֶשׁ כִּ֤י רָאוּ֙ בַּאֲר֣וֹן יְהוָ֔ה וַיַּ֤ךְ בָּעָם֙ שִׁבְעִ֣ים אִ֔ישׁ חֲמִשִּׁ֥ים אֶ֖לֶף אִ֑ישׁ וַיִּֽתְאַבְּל֣וּ הָעָ֔ם כִּֽי־הִכָּ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה בָּעָ֖ם מַכָּ֥ה גְדוֹלָֽה

records.literal_gloss: And he struck among [the] men of Beth-shemesh, because they looked into [the] ark of Yahweh, and he struck among the people seventy men, fifty thousand men; and mourned the people, because struck Yahweh among the people a great blow.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} struck among the men of Beth-shemesh, because they looked into the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} struck among the people seventy men, 50,000 men. And the people mourned, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had struck among the people [with] a great blow.
en.B: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} struck down some of the men of Beth-shemesh for looking into the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. He struck down seventy men among the people, 50,000 men. The people mourned because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had struck them with such a heavy blow.
en.R: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} struck down some of the men of Beth-shemesh, because they had looked inside {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} ark. He killed seventy men among the people, 50,000 men. The people mourned because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had struck them so hard.

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} hirió entre los hombres de Bet-semes, porque miraron dentro del arca {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}; e hirió entre el pueblo a setenta hombres, 50 000 hombres. Y el pueblo hizo duelo, porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} había herido al pueblo [con] un gran golpe.
es.B: Pero {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} hirió a algunos de los hombres de Bet-semes por haber mirado dentro del arca {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}. Hirió de muerte a setenta hombres del pueblo, 50 000 hombres. El pueblo hizo duelo porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} lo había herido con un golpe tan duro.
es.R: Pero {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} hirió de muerte a algunos de los hombres de Bet-semes, porque habían mirado dentro de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} arca. Mató a setenta hombres del pueblo, 50 000 hombres. La gente hizo duelo porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} los había castigado con tanta dureza.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} frappa parmi les hommes de Beth-Shémesh, parce qu’ils avaient regardé dans l’arche {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} ; et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} frappa parmi le peuple soixante-dix hommes, cinquante mille hommes. Et le peuple fut dans le deuil, parce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} avait frappé parmi le peuple [d’]un grand coup.
fr.B: Mais {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} frappa des hommes de Beth-Shémesh parce qu’ils avaient regardé dans l’arche {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. Il frappa soixante-dix hommes parmi le peuple, cinquante mille hommes. Le peuple prit le deuil parce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} l’avait frappé d’un coup si terrible.
fr.R: Mais {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a frappé des hommes de Beth-Shémesh, parce qu’ils avaient regardé à l’intérieur de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} arche. Il a fait mourir soixante-dix hommes parmi le peuple, cinquante mille hommes. Le peuple a pris le deuil, parce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} l’avait frappé si durement.

vi.L: Ngài đánh giữa vòng người Bết-Sê-mết, vì họ đã nhìn vào hòm của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}; {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đánh giữa vòng dân bảy mươi người, năm mươi nghìn người. Dân chúng than khóc, vì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã giáng [một] đòn nặng nề giữa vòng dân.
vi.B: Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đánh chết một số người Bết-Sê-mết vì họ đã nhìn vào hòm của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. Ngài đánh chết bảy mươi người trong dân, năm mươi nghìn người. Dân chúng than khóc vì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã giáng trên họ một đòn nặng nề như thế.
vi.R: Nhưng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đánh chết một số người Bết-Sê-mết, vì họ đã nhìn vào trong hòm của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Ngài giết bảy mươi người trong dân, năm mươi nghìn người. Dân chúng than khóc vì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã đánh phạt họ nặng nề như vậy.

decisions.choice: he struck the men of Beth-shemesh because they looked into the ark
alternatives: the sons of Jeconiah did not rejoice ... and he struck among them
decisions.reason: The ancient Greek translation begins differently: "And the sons of Jeconiah did not rejoice with the men of Beth-shemesh when they saw the ark of the Lord, and he struck them." On that reading one family is punished for not joining in. The Hebrew text is followed here.

decisions.choice: looked into: gazed at or into what was holy
decisions.reason: The words can mean "looked at" or "looked into"; either way they treated the holy ark as something to stare at. Even the Levites of Kohath were not to look at the holy things or they would die (Numbers 4:20).

decisions.choice: seventy men, fifty thousand men: the Hebrew as it stands, with its difficulty kept
decisions.reason: The Hebrew sets "seventy men" and "fifty thousand men" side by side with no "and", which is not how Hebrew normally adds numbers, and Beth-shemesh was a small town. Some Hebrew manuscripts and the Jewish historian Josephus have only seventy, and many think "fifty thousand men" was added to the text later. Others read the two as one total (50,070), or as seventy men out of fifty thousand, or take the word for "thousand" as a clan or military unit (see the note at Numbers 1:21), which would give a much smaller number. The text is kept as it is so the reader can see the problem.

decisions.choice: Yahweh struck: the holiness of the ark cut both ways
decisions.reason: The ark that had brought plague on the Philistines brought death to Israelites who did not treat it as holy. The same lesson returns when Uzzah touches the ark (2 Samuel 6:6-7).

decisions.choice: struck down some of; the LORD (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Struck among" means some of them, not all, which Balanced and Readable say. Readable names the LORD as the one who struck, since the Hebrew names him only at the end of the verse.

source.text: וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ אַנְשֵׁ֣י בֵֽית־שֶׁ֔מֶשׁ מִ֚י יוּכַ֣ל לַעֲמֹ֔ד לִפְנֵ֨י יְהוָ֧ה הָאֱלֹהִ֛ים הַקָּד֖וֹשׁ הַזֶּ֑ה וְאֶל־מִ֖י יַעֲלֶ֥ה מֵעָלֵֽינוּ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And said [the] men of Beth-shemesh, Who is able to stand before Yahweh, the God, the holy, this? And to whom will he go up from us?

en.L: And the men of Beth-shemesh said, "Who is able to stand before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, this holy God? And to whom will {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} go up from us?"
en.B: Then the men of Beth-shemesh asked, "Who is able to stand before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, this holy God? And to whom should {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} go up from here, away from us?"
en.R: The men of Beth-shemesh said, "No one can stand before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, this holy God! Where can we send {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will go away from us?"

es.L: Y los hombres de Bet-semes dijeron: «¿Quién podrá estar en pie delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, este Dios santo? ¿Y a quién subirá {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} desde nosotros?».
es.B: Entonces los hombres de Bet-semes preguntaron: «¿Quién puede estar en pie delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, este Dios santo? ¿Y a quién subirá desde aquí, lejos de nosotros?».
es.R: Los hombres de Bet-semes dijeron: «¡Nadie puede estar delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, este Dios santo! ¿Adónde podemos enviarlo para que se aleje de nosotros?».

fr.L: Et les hommes de Beth-Shémesh dirent : « Qui peut se tenir devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, ce Dieu saint ? Et vers qui montera-t-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}}, [loin] de nous ? »
fr.B: Les hommes de Beth-Shémesh se demandèrent alors : « Qui peut tenir devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, ce Dieu saint ? Et chez qui doit-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} monter, loin de nous ? »
fr.R: Les hommes de Beth-Shémesh ont dit : « Personne ne peut rester devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, ce Dieu saint ! Où pouvons-nous {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}envoyer pour qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} s’éloigne de nous ? »

vi.L: Người Bết-Sê-mết nói: "Ai có thể đứng trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời thánh khiết này? Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ đi lên khỏi chúng ta đến với ai?"
vi.B: Người Bết-Sê-mết hỏi: "Ai có thể đứng trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời thánh khiết này? Ngài nên đi lên từ đây đến với ai, cho khỏi chúng ta?"
vi.R: Người Bết-Sê-mết nói: "Không ai có thể đứng trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời thánh khiết này! Chúng ta có thể đưa {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đi đâu để {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} rời khỏi chúng ta?"

decisions.choice: who can stand before Yahweh, this holy God: no one can bear his presence
decisions.reason: To stand before Yahweh is to be in his presence or to serve him there, as the Levites did (Deuteronomy 10:8). The men see that his holiness is dangerous to anyone who treats it lightly.

decisions.choice: he will go up: Yahweh, present with his ark
decisions.reason: The verb can also be read "it will go up", meaning the ark. The two are closely joined in the story, since the ark stood for Yahweh's presence (4:7). Either way, they want it taken away from them, up to another town.

decisions.choice: a statement and a plain question
decisions.reason: Readable turns the first question into the statement it implies and makes the second a practical question about where to send him.

source.text: וַֽיִּשְׁלְחוּ֙ מַלְאָכִ֔ים אֶל־יוֹשְׁבֵ֥י קִרְיַת־יְעָרִ֖ים לֵאמֹ֑ר הֵשִׁ֤בוּ פְלִשְׁתִּים֙ אֶת־אֲר֣וֹן יְהוָ֔ה רְד֕וּ הַעֲל֥וּ אֹת֖וֹ אֲלֵיכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And they sent messengers to [the] inhabitants of Kiriath-jearim, saying, [The] Philistines have brought back [the] ark of Yahweh; come down, bring it up to you.

en.L: And they sent messengers to the inhabitants of Kiriath-jearim, saying, "[The] Philistines have brought back the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Come down; bring it up to you."
en.B: So they sent messengers to the people of Kiriath-jearim to say, "The Philistines have brought back the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Come down and carry it up to your town."
en.R: Then they sent messengers to the people who lived in Kiriath-jearim. The messengers said, "The Philistines have sent back the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Come down here and take it up to your town."

es.L: Y enviaron mensajeros a los habitantes de Quiriat-jearim, diciendo: «[Los] filisteos han devuelto el arca {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}. {{plural_you:Desciendan|Descended}}; {{plural_you:súbanla|subidla}} a donde {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} [están]».
es.B: Así que enviaron mensajeros a los habitantes de Quiriat-jearim para decirles: «Los filisteos han devuelto el arca {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}. {{plural_you:Bajen|Bajad}} y {{plural_you:llévensela|lleváosla}} a {{plural_you:su ciudad|vuestra ciudad}}».
es.R: Entonces enviaron mensajeros a la gente que vivía en Quiriat-jearim. Los mensajeros dijeron: «Los filisteos han devuelto el arca {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}. {{plural_you:Bajen|Bajad}} aquí y {{plural_you:llévensela|lleváosla}} a {{plural_you:su pueblo|vuestro pueblo}}».

fr.L: Et ils envoyèrent des messagers aux habitants de Qiryath-Yearim, en disant : « Les Philistins ont ramené l’arche {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} ; descendez, faites-la monter chez vous. »
fr.B: Ils envoyèrent donc des messagers aux habitants de Qiryath-Yearim pour leur dire : « Les Philistins ont ramené l’arche {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. Descendez et faites-la monter chez vous. »
fr.R: Alors ils ont envoyé des messagers aux habitants de Qiryath-Yearim. Les messagers ont dit : « Les Philistins ont renvoyé l’arche {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. Descendez ici et emportez-la dans votre ville. »

vi.L: Họ sai sứ giả đến cùng dân cư Ki-ri-át Giê-a-rim mà nói: "Người Phi-li-tin đã đem trả hòm của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. Hãy xuống, đem hòm lên với các anh."
vi.B: Vậy họ sai sứ giả đến nói với dân Ki-ri-át Giê-a-rim: "Người Phi-li-tin đã đem trả hòm của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. Hãy xuống đây khiêng hòm lên thành các anh."
vi.R: Rồi họ sai sứ giả đến với dân sống ở Ki-ri-át Giê-a-rim. Các sứ giả nói: "Người Phi-li-tin đã gửi trả hòm của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. Hãy xuống đây đem hòm lên thành của các anh."

decisions.choice: Kiriath-jearim: a town in the hills to the northeast of Beth-shemesh
decisions.reason: Kiriath-jearim stood higher up, in the hills toward Jerusalem (Joshua 9:17; 15:9), so the people come "down" and take the ark "up". The ark stayed there until David brought it to Jerusalem (7:1-2; 2 Samuel 6:2).

decisions.choice: the message: good news of the ark's return, with nothing said of the deaths
decisions.reason: The men of Beth-shemesh tell only that the ark is back and ask the other town to take it.

decisions.choice: to your town
decisions.reason: "Up to you" means up to where they live.

decisions.choice: "Ki-ri-át Giê-a-rim"
decisions.reason: As the Samuel terms note.
